page: Microsoft Azure EC2es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical Intel Xeon TDX core running at 4.2 GHz with 2 threads per core on an x86_64 architecture. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and access to 260 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8), VAES, and SHA-NI for vector math, AI matrix acceleration, and cryptographic operations.

Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB RAM, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio aligned with standard memory-optimized cloud baselines. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPUs, requiring reliance on remote managed disk volumes such as Azure Premium Storage for persistent workloads. Network operations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-thread execution coupled with modest overall parallel capacity due to the 2-vCPU ceiling. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1943.0, placing in the top quartile, and a stress-ng single-core score of 1904.76. Multi-core performance is constrained, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 2182.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 1962.27. Memory-focused tests returned a PassMark memory score of 1687.6, while Redis SET throughput reached 2.58 million operations per second.

Because the configuration trades total parallel compute capacity for high RAM density per core, it offers cost-efficient scaling for low-concurrency, memory-heavy workloads. The profile is well suited for dedicated in-memory caching tiers, small enterprise relational databases, lightweight staging environments, and single-threaded data processing applications that require substantial memory headroom without massive compute scaling.

There is no bundled local storage or integrated GPU, necessitating attached remote storage volumes. In memory benchmarks, Redis SET performance achieved 2.58 million operations per second alongside modest PassMark memory results. Azure EC2es_v6 is technically suited for small database engines, in-memory key-value caches, lightweight analytics tasks, and background job runners that require moderate compute paired with generous memory allocations.
